newsitem.title: USA: US debt futures end lower, but above Monday's lows.
newsitem.headline: US debt futures end lower, but above Monday's lows.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed lower on a late selloff that was sparked by heavy corporate supply, traders said.
However, they also noted June T-bonds and June Eurodollars limited losses above Monday's pit lows of 109-24/32 and 94.16, respectively. June Eurodollars held support at 94.17.

Several major U.S. dealers each sold 1,000 June bonds when the contract fell through 110-00. The 110-00 level proved to be resilient support for most of the day until a corporate bid list rumored at $1.4 billion from a West Coast fund manager did not spark demand for T-bond instruments, they said.
"We were anticipating bidding well into the close, and it didn't happen," one bond futures trader said.
In fact, he said the bid list drew hedging pressure as dealers who bought corporate paper sold T-notes and T-bonds.

Several traders noted that selling pressure on the floor started with five-year note futures, which then spilled into the T-bond futures pit. They said that while long term corporate bonds were well absorbed, there was mediocre demand for intermediate term paper.
One dealer alone sold 1,500 June bonds at 109-30/32, while another firm sold 500 at 109-28/32.

One trader thought in the final minutes of trade that June bonds would fall through 109-24/32, and possibly test the 200-day moving average at 109-21/32. Some analysts pegged the 200-day moving average at 109-26/32.
They also attributed late declines to jitters ahead of the second leg of U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday.
For most of the day, June bonds and Eurodollars held a slight upward bias and drifted in tight narrow ranges.
Neither Greenspan's comments on the budget, nor a $1.438 billion Fed coupon pass, broke the market's sideways grasp.
"There is just no momentum down here," one trader said at midday.
Greenspan said Tuesday that investors remain somewhat skeptical about the ability of Congress and the Clinton administration to strike a convincing budget deal that would reduce the deficit.
He also argued that the consumer price index significantly overstates inflation, and said it was "crucial" to keep inflation down in the near term.
Greenspan also defended his recent cautionary remarks about the steep run-up in the U.S. stock market.
Traders said the 2.4 percent increase in U.S. Redbook retail sales for the first four weeks of fiscal February versus January had little effect on the market.
They said rise was close to trade expectations.

At the end of pit trade, June T-bonds were off 11/32 points at 109-26/32, 10-year notes fell 07/32 to 107-12/32, munibonds were down 06/32 at 113-26/32, June T-bills were off 0.010 basis point to 94.735, and June Eurodollars were off 0.005 to 94.18.
